To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have generated a monoclonal B-cell hybridoma that can be stimulated to secrete antibody by antigen.
we generated a monoclonal antigen-responsive hybridoma by fusing a hapten-specific antibody-secreting cell with a non-secreting pre-B cell tumor line.

a monoclonal B cell hybrid has been generated by fusion of a pre-B cell line and an antibody-secreting tumor cell, which can be induced by a haptenated Lymphosaccharide (LPS) to secrete specific antibody.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of monoclonal antibodies to specific antigens and the use of these reagents for the study of cell surface differentiation antigens and receptors.
the molecular and cellular basis for antibody diversity, the mechanisms by which antigen stimulates the production of antibodies and the molecular basis for B cell activation.
the study of the molecular mechanisms involved in the differentiation of the B lymphocyte into an antibody-secreting cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a B-cell tumor has been fused with another B-cell tumor to produce a third tumor which is capable of responding to antigenic stimulation by secreting specific antibody.
a hybridoma was generated that was capable of responding to a specific antigen by producing antibodies, but only in response to a specific haptenated LIP.
a hybrid cell line has been produced which is specific for fluorescein and which can be stimulated to produce antibodies to this hapten.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the generation of a monoclonally derived, specific B-cell line has been achieved, which can be induced to secrete antibody by a hapten-specific stimulus, and which can be maintained indefinitely in culture.
a B-cell hybridoma has been produced which can be stimulated by antigen to secrete specific antibody.
we have developed a hybridoma cell line which is antigen-responsive and which secretes specific antibody upon stimulation with the appropriate antigen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that it is possible to create a hybridoma cell line that can be activated by an antigen.
we have shown that a B cell line can be made to secrete specific antibody upon stimulation with antigen, and that the response to the antigen is specific and can be measured quantitatively.

the hybridoma technology can be extended to generate antigen-specific, but nonsecretory hybridomas, which can serve a useful purpose in the analysis of the mechanisms underlying B-cell differentiation.
